patches.rationale: The original test `test_malformed_future_timestamp` expects that when the decoded timestamp is out of datetime's supported range on the invalid-signature path, the raised BadTimeSignature message contains "Malformed". The current code raises BadTimeSignature with `str(sig_error)` (the signature-mismatch message) even when the timestamp conversion fails. The fix: when the timestamp conversion fails on the invalid-signature path, raise BadTimeSignature with a "Malformed timestamp" message (still carrying the original payload and date_signed=None). Ordinary invalid signatures with in-range timestamps keep the signature-error message and decoded date_signed. Valid roundtrips, expiry, and the serializer contract are untouched. New regression tests are added in a NEW file to avoid editing existing tests.

patches.rationale: The failure_diagnostics shows an existing test `test_malformed_future_timestamp` in tests/test_itsdangerous/test_timed.py expects `"Malformed" in str(exc_info.value)` for the signed value `b"value.TgPVoaGhoQ.AGBfQ6G6cr07byTRt0zAdPljHOY"`. That timestamp decodes to an out-of-range value, so the invalid-signature path must raise BadTimeSignature with a "Malformed timestamp" message (not the raw signature-mismatch message). The current source already wraps the conversion, but the message must be "Malformed timestamp" and the payload must be the original payload. I'll ensure the source raises BadTimeSignature("Malformed timestamp", payload=value, date_signed=None) on the invalid-signature path when conversion fails, and add a NEW regression test file covering all acceptance contracts.
